Design Palette

Design Book

1,220 sq ft · 2 bed / 3 bath

A black-and-white checkerboard floor, set on the diagonal, runs through the entire home — bedrooms, both upstairs bathrooms, living room, kitchen, dining room, entryways, closets — at one consistent size throughout, stopping only at the downstairs bath, where a small-format white mosaic takes the whole floor, paired with glossy white-gray walls and matte black hardware. The primary bedroom gets a pair of twin beds, plus a power recline love seat. The secondary bedroom gets full bed. The downstairs powder room is converted into a full bath with a curbless corner shower, and the living room gets a matching power recline sofa and storage coffee table.

By Room Material callouts and specifications
Primary Bedroom

Two separate twin beds give the kids who sleep here their own space. A power recline sleeper love seat sits between them for guests. The 13-foot wall behind both headboards and the sofa is wrapped floor to ceiling in the same wood-look plank tile used on the entryway wall, run vertically in 13 columns to pull the eye up — a durable, wipeable surface right where beds and furniture make contact. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish elsewhere in the room. Closets stay open — doors come off, frames stay in place — fitted with built-in organizers and a built-in desktop. All hardware in matte black.

Reference image — wood slat accent wall behind a bed, paired with black hardware (sconces, nightstands, lamp). Same wood-slat language used elsewhere in the house; not a locked spec, just a mood reference.

Primary Bathroom

Alcove tub / tile shower with matte black drain kit, right drain, and a curved shower curtain rod. Deep emerald ceramic in a glossy glaze, laid vertically in stacked columns, wraps the tub surround and carries straight on down the whole wall that holds the vanity and toilet, floor to ceiling — one continuous plane rather than a patch behind the mirror. Single 36" vanity, Acorn finish, black hardware provides unobstructed width to the tub's full alcove opening. Checkerboard floor, gray walls, matte black faucet, medicine cabinet, toilet, shower head + handheld wand for tub use.

Dining Room

Checkerboard floors, gray walls in glossy finish. Kitchen cabinets and counters extend across the length of the dining room with 36" counter depth to allow use as desk space at bar stool height and space to put a coffee machine. Dining table is 36" round dining table (white marble top, matte black base), paired with 4 black ash dining chairs. Downstairs Bathroom

Powder room converted to a full bath. The floor changes at the threshold: the checkerboard stops at the door and a dark charcoal small-format mosaic takes over the whole room, running straight into the shower — the shower floor sits flush with the room floor, no curb to step over. The shower sits in one corner, roughly 30 by 36 inches, with a slot drain hidden against the wall behind it rather than a round drain in the middle of the floor. There's no glass and no door: the shower's two open sides are wrapped by a single matte black L-shaped rod anchored to the outside corner of the same two walls that carry the tile, with a plain curtain hung around the bend — nothing to swing, nothing to leave a wet-corner puddle where a hinge would otherwise sit. The same wood-look plank tile used in the bedrooms and entryway wraps the shower's own two walls, laid vertically, ending at the curtain rod. Everywhere else in the room stays glossy gray. The toilet sits in its own corner facing into the room, and the corner sink keeps its spot near the entry. A tall recessed niche is set into the shower wall with the flutes carrying straight through it, so it reads as part of the wall rather than a hole cut in it. Matte black rain head and handheld wand, the same pair used in both suite baths. A matte black single-hole faucet sits on the corner sink, with a compact medicine cabinet above and the same toilet used elsewhere in the house. A pocket door at the entry means nothing swings into this small room at all.

Reference image — wood-look plank taken floor to ceiling against a dark small-format mosaic floor, close to this room's scheme. Fittings shown are brass over a patterned mosaic; ours are matte black over a plain charcoal one.

Floor plan reference (1.7m x 1.8m) — this is close to the actual arrangement: shower and WC sharing one wall with a basin near the entry. Our room is 61" x 61", the shower is 30" x 36" and curbless, with a slot drain hidden against the wall rather than a round drain in the open floor, and one mosaic floor runs through the whole room including the shower.

Entryway

An archway passageway wall between the living room and kitchen, not a mudroom or front-door landing zone — no hooks, no shoe storage, since this is a walk-through space, not somewhere people pause. Checkerboard floors, gray walls elsewhere in the room. The wall gets a wood-look ribbed ceramic in a plank format, wrapping up and over the small ceiling section above it too — no art or cabinet breaking it up, the tile carries the whole surface as one clean statement. A long uninterrupted dry wall is exactly what the plank proportion and the relief texture need to read properly.

Stairs

Connecting space between the living room and bedrooms upstairs. Reclaimed hardwood treads, milled with a built-up roundover nose, stained to the walnut tone used by the bedroom furniture and finished in a hard multi-coat clear, over white-painted risers. Walls confirmed gray, glossy finish. All railings and hardware in matte black.

Reference image — the scheme in use: diagonal checkerboard floor running into stained wood treads over white risers, with a black balustrade. Mood reference, not a locked spec.

Under-Stairs Walk-In Closet

Same footprint that used to be a walk-in pantry, now framed as a generic walk-in closet — a mix of hanging rods and open shelving, a wall-mounted vacuum charging dock, and a dedicated light fixture (previously unlit). If the household ever needs food storage instead, the shelving works equally well for that — general-purpose storage either way. Checkerboard floor, gray walls in glossy finish, matte black hardware.

Reference image — narrow closet layout with dedicated zones (double-hang, drawers/shelves, long-hang) plus shoe shelving on the back wall. Mood/layout reference, not a locked spec.

Edward Martin Leona, Calacatta + Nero Marquina, matte

Gray Matters SW 7066, actual sample

A note on flexibility. The one must-have is the checkerboard tile throughout. Everything else — colors, materials, fixtures, and how to get the best value — is genuinely open to the design firm's judgment. This palette is a starting reference, not a locked spec. The general aesthetic direction we're after: fresh and current, the kind of space that photographs well today, but grounded enough in timeless choices that it won't read as dated in five or ten years.
